title.narrative: Second Inclusive and Resilient Market Economy Development Policy Operation

description.narrative: The development objective of the Second Inclusive and Resilient Market Economy Development Policy Operation for Uzbekistan is to support Uzbekistan's transition to an inclusive and resilient market economy through: (i) creating markets, (ii) improving fiscal risk management and public procurement, and (iii) supporting social inclusion and climate change action. The operation supports key government priorities. The first program development objective (PDO) pillar supports measures to improve the business and investment environment, and to enhance efficiency and reduce state dominance in the key sectors of agriculture, rail, and energy. The second pillar supports measures to improve fiscal risk management, especially relating to public-private partnership (PPPs) and public procurement. The third pillar supports measures to expand in-work social protection, further measures to protect victims of domestic violence, and measures to strengthen environmental sustainability and climate change action.

To support Uzbekistan's transition to an inclusive and resilient market economy through: (i) creating markets, (ii) improving fiscal risk management and public procurement, and (iii) supporting social inclusion and climate change action.

comment.narrative: Greenhouse gas emissions intensity per GDP unit (using 2011 dollars) decreased ahead of target, from 2.55 kg (measured by old methodology CO2eq/US$ in 2011 dollars) in 2017 (baseline) to 2.35 in 2023 (intermediate), surpassing the 2026 target of 2.42 by 11 percent ahead of the schedule. Alternatively, using the updated indicator cited in the Biennial Report on Transparency of the Republic of Uzbekistan Under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (CO2eq/US$ using 2015 dollars instead of 2011 dollars; baseline: 1.8 kg in December 2017; Intermediate target: 1.69 kg in December 2024) also shows significant progress from the baseline.

title.narrative: Number of newly registered foreign companies per year

comment.narrative: The intermediate result indicator has already exceeded the target—3,658 enterprises with foreign investment were registered as of October 2025, 2.9 times more than the baseline in 2022 (1,249 enterprises) and above the target of 1,374 enterprises by December 2026. Most of newly registered foreign enterprises were established in industry, and mostly by China, Russia, Turkiye, Kazakhstan, and South Korea.

title.narrative: Share of state supported investments that conform with the Green Taxonomy

comment.narrative: There has been no data collected to confirm progress towards this indicator. The delay on increasing investments that conform with Green Taxonomy is of concern because the Cabinet of Ministers decree “On approval of national green taxonomy” (No. up-561 from October 25, 2023) states that in adopting the Green Taxonomy, by October 1, 2024 “The investment expenditures of all business entities, including private and public economic entities, that will have received state financial support (subsidies, grants, credit lines, guarantees, etc.) will be classified based on the national "green" economy taxonomy, and a procedure will be introduced for them to submit information to the responsible republican executive body.”

title.narrative: Number of companies in the chemical sector with a majority of private ownership

comment.narrative: The intermediate result indicator has already hit the target ahead of time – two chemical plants have been privatized with a majority of private ownership: Ferganaazot, in May 2023, and Dekhkanabad Potash Plant, in August 2025.

title.narrative: Reduction in air pollutants emitted by industrial sources relative to 2022 (%by weight)

comment.narrative: Intermediate indicator demonstrates some progress in air pollution reduction by 0.8 percent as of December 2024 compared to December 2022. To achieve the target of 6 percent air pollution reduction by December 2026, however, the performance must accelerate.

title.narrative: Land productivity index 2022=100 (agriculture value added in real terms in billion sums per 1000 hectare of sown area)

comment.narrative: The intermediate indicator shows the implementation of reforms is on-track as land productivity as of June 2025 reached 112.5 from the level of December 2022, and given current trend, it is expected to reach the target of 115 of 2022 level by December 2026.

title.narrative: Share of poorest quantile receiving at least one type of social protection support

comment.narrative: In August 2025 the Bank social protection team has recalculated the baseline for this indicator using household budget survey data and indicated that it needs to be adjusted slightly from the level of 79.0 percent (indicated in the Program Document) to 78.6 percent; accordingly the target for this indicator also needs to be adjusted from initial 85.0 percent to 84.6 percent reflecting the updated measurement of the baseline. The Bank social protection team believes that 84.6 percent (proposed updated indicator instead of 85 percent) coverage target for end-2026 remains achievable, though implementation of this reform needs urgent attention. In fact, as of March 2023 (intermediate indicator) only 77.7 percent of the poorest quintile received some form of social assistance (i.e. slightly below 78.6 percent baseline of March 2022). Efforts are underway to address exclusion errors in cash transfer programs, improve HBS survey questionnaires to capture all relevant programs.

title.narrative: Share of total public procurement that is: 1) subject to competitive, electronic means, ii) green public procurement

comment.narrative: Competitive electronic procurement increased from 43.6 percent in 2022 to 52 percent as of September 2025, with green public procurement rising from 0 percent to 22 percent, with targets by end-2026 of 60 percent and 15 percent, respectively.

title.narrative: Share of the labor force contributing to the new social insurance schemes

comment.narrative: This intermediate indicator is still at zero as of December 2025 as the draft Law on social insurance has passed the Oliy Majlis (lower chamber of Parliament) and is under review in the Senate (upper chamber of the Parliament).

title.narrative: Energy tariffs recovering portion of their costs

baseline.value: Electricity - 61% cost recovery, natural gas - 44% cost recovery

target.value: Electricity and natural gas - 100% cost recovery

comment.narrative: Intermediate indicator shows that electricity and natural gas cost recovery rates have significantly increased (on electricity – 92 percent, and on natural gas – 83 percent cost recovery), moving towards full cost recovery by 2026.

actual.value: Electricity - 92% cost recovery, natural gas - 83% cost recovery

title.narrative: Existence of a budgeted PSA with key performance indicators

target.value: PSA with key performance indicators presented in the public budget

comment.narrative: The Ministry of Transport has approved the contractual framework for the first Public Service Agreement (PSA) through a Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers No. 425 dated July 16, 2024. No PSA agreement was expected in 2024 and in 2025. The first PSA is scheduled to be launched from July to December 2026. However, if a PSA would be finalized before that date, there is a temporary arrangement for 2026 to subsidize the costs of one PSA from the state budget. The World Bank is providing technical assistance to UTY on reforming its tariffs (start date: November 2025). This serves as a precursor to a Public Service Agreement (PSA) and Multi-Annual Infrastructure Contracts (MAIC).

title.narrative: Fiscal risk framework and publication of report on contingent liabilities from PPPs

baseline.value: No fiscal framework or methodology and no report on contingent liabilities from PPPs

target.value: Approved fiscal framework, adopted methodology for fiscal risks assessment and management and at least 2 fiscal risk reports covering PPP contingent liabilities

comment.narrative: Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Uzbekistan “On the approval of the regulation on managing the state's fiscal obligations arising from public-private partnership projects” was adopted (October 23, 2023, No 558) that establishes a unified framework for managing the state's direct and contingent fiscal obligations arising from PPP projects that are ongoing, planned, or at the preparation/tender stage. It sets out procedures for analyzing, approving, and monitoring such obligations under the authority of the Ministry of Economy and Finance. To date, two Fiscal Risk Reports have been published: (1) In May 2024, the government released its first-ever Fiscal Risk Statement, which reported the value of the state's direct obligations under 182 major PPP projects for 2024, along with forward-looking projections, and (2) in July 2025, as required by the Budget Code of Uzbekistan, the Fiscal Strategy for 2026–2028 (https://gov.uz/en/imv/news/view/73599) has been prepared and published.

actual.value: Approved fiscal framework, adopted methodology for fiscal risks assessment and management, and 2 fiscal risk reports published (in May 2024 and July 2025) covering PPP contingent liabilities

title.narrative: Share of social protection recipients that are below the ‘social norm’ for: i) electricity; ii) gas (during heating season)

baseline.value: Electricity - 0% of social protection recipients, natural gas - 0% of social protection recipients

target.value: Electricity and natural gas - 70% of social protection recipients

comment.narrative: The intermediate indicator demonstrates the achievement of the target level ahead of schedule. According to the National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of Uzbekistan, the intermediate indicator shows that target of 70 percent by the end-2026 was already achieved in January 2025 (during heating season), ahead of schedule, on electricity (89 percent recipients of social assistance programs) and on natural gas (98 percent recipients of social assistance programs). Social workers of NASP went to all the people in the single registry and other vulnerable categories and asked them to apply to the subsidy, i.e. compensation for those consuming above the social norm for electricity and gas. The denominator in this ratio is all low-income family allowance recipients plus those extra people identified as vulnerable. The numerator in this ratio is those receiving compensation, and out of those who applied, all who meet the consumption criteria have got compensation.

actual.value: Electricity - 89% recipients of social assistance programs; natural gas – 98% recipients of social assistance programs

title.narrative: Percentage of GBV cases filed, including domestic and sexual violence, that receive a verdict protecting survivors

comment.narrative: Intermediate indicator of 12.4 percent as of August 2025 demonstrates progress compared to 5 percent in the baseline in 2022.

title.narrative: GHG emission reductions from energy efficiency measures at major emitters (25 largest SOEs)

comment.narrative: The GHG emission reduction of 1.53 million tCO2 (annualized) was achieved by June 2025 , surpassing the 2026 target of 1.5 million tCO2. To achieve this, the authorities used the green economy measures (Presidential decree No.436 from December 2022) which instructed agencies to take sector and economy-wide actions. Thanks to these efforts, they have managed to improve energy efficiency in industry, buildings, and end-user gas consumption. Part of this is due to tariff reforms (facilitated by the DPO and sector projects), part from investments (e.g., CEBU project), and part from the introduction of green standards and targets. The energy generation sector has also increased its share of renewable energy and energy efficiency in industries more generally.

title.narrative: Number of water management balances prepared for river basins incorporating the effects of climate change and published

comment.narrative: The Water Code of Uzbekistan was approved on July 30, 2025 (Law # 1076) and entered into force in November 2025. Article 20 stipulates the development of water balances for river basins. Thus, as legal basis to prepare water balances is now in place, the national water agencies started developing the regulation to implement the law through drafting methodologies on how to prepare respective water balances for river basins and started receiving funding from MEF on these works.
